message.reasoning:
The user wants to see community posted comments about slack.com from VirusTotal. They want the next 30 comments using cursor 'slack_c2'. They provide an API key sl_key456.

We need to call the VirusTotal API. The user wants community posted comments about slack.com. That would be the endpoint: GET /api/v3/comments?resource=slack.com&cursor=slack_c2&limit=30. We need to include the API key in the header or query param. According to VirusTotal API v3, the API key can be passed as a query parameter 'apikey' or as a header 'x-apikey'.

We need to construct the request. The user didn't specify whether we should use the API key as a header or query param. We'll choose header 'x-apikey'.

We need to produce a JSON request body? Actually it's a GET request, so no body. But we need to produce a JSON representation of the request. The user said: "If you need to make an API call, you should do it in JSON format." So we need to output a JSON object with fields: method, url, headers, params, body. The body can be omitted or empty.

We need to include the API key. Let's include it in the header 'x-apikey': 'sl_key456'.

We also need to include the resource 'slack.com', cursor 'slack_c2', limit 30. These can be query parameters.

So the JSON request:

{
  "method": "GET",
  "url": "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/comments",
  "headers": {
    "x-apikey": "sl_key456"
  },
  "params": {
    "resource": "slack.com",
    "cursor": "slack_c2",
    "limit": 30
  }
}

We don't need a body. So we can omit body or set it to null.

We should not include any other keys. The user didn't ask for anything else.

Thus we output the JSON.
